thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HOSTED eu-west-1 - kvcache memory anomaly detected on shard-12. heap trending to OOM (95% -> warning). alerts triggered and partial failures starting.

sarah: spotted repeated sessions with huge evolving prefixes, some sessions sending incremental updates that balloon the KV index. noticed spikes at 11:07 UTC.

miguel: logs show continuous-batching windows expanding unbounded; one stream pushed concatenated prefixes up to ~58k tokens. GC doesn't reclaim due to refcounting lag.

priya: any immediate customer impact? which routes?

ben: small fraction of request failures, mostly generation/chat endpoints for long-context models. error-rate peaked ~1.8% on shard-12; overall region tail latency up 3-4x for affected paths.

emily: routing queues filling; health checks showing backpressure. risk of cascading if not contained.

miguel: preliminary cause: continuous-batching merge logic concatenates incremental prefix events without enforcing dedupe or max-prefix-size. also saw a race where session flush not triggered, leaving stale entries.

priya: mitigation choices: A) flip runtime flag to cap per-session prefetch tokens to 12k; B) temporary disable continuous-batching on shard-12; C) run immediate eviction sweep removing keys >90s old; D) apply emergency per-session key limit. Thoughts?

ben: do minimal blast radius: enable caps via config flag on shard-12 then fire eviction. if that stabilizes, rollback to controlled state.

emily: agree. do config flag first. prefer targeted change to avoid affecting global hosted performance.

priya: @deploy-bot please push config change: runtime.kvcache.prefetch_max_tokens=12000 and runtime.batch.max_context_tokens=12000 scoped to shard-12. include rollback token in the change.

deploy-bot: Applying config update on hosts matching shard-12: set prefetch_max_tokens and batch.max_context_tokens. ticket 9001-hotcap.

incident-bot: CONFIG APPLIED (11:12 UTC) on shard-12.

miguel: immediate telemetry: memory usage trending down 95% -> 70% within 40s. error-rate declining. good indicator.

priya: next step: kick off KV eviction for stale keys older than 90s on shard-12 to free fragmented allocations. ben please run safe-evict.

ben: running safe-evict now:
```
POST /internal/kvcache/evict
{"shard":"shard-12","older_than_s":90,"dry_run":false}
```

ben: eviction completed. reclaimed ~7% of heap. no new 5xxs in last 90s.

emily: still seeing slow finishes for a handful of the very-long sessions but no new enqueues. overall region health improving.

priya: assign owners: miguel (runtime) for fix & tests, ben (ops) for runbook adjustments, sarah (cs) for customer comms. put monitoring on 2h watch.

incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by oncall (priya). Status -> mitigated, monitoring.

customer-success: two customers impacted intermittently; preparing a short note.

sarah: draft to customers: "We observed transient errors for a small subset of long-context requests in eu-west-1. We applied a safety cap and cleared stale cache entries; traffic is stable and we continue monitoring. No user data was lost. We'll follow up with a root-cause and hard fix."

miguel: root-cause hypothesis: continuous-batching merge path allowed repeated prefetch re-insertions without dedupe, and refcount decrement only occurred on explicit session close. follow-ups: add dedupe at prefetch merge, ensure refcount decrements on partial flush, add unit/integration tests, and add telemetry for per-session KV growth rates.

ben: ops follow-ups: create an emergency runbook for kvcache growth spikes: auto-apply caps, targeted evict, and trigger high-sensitivity alert if single session accounts for >40% of prefetch keys over 30s.

priya: scheduling: SEV-2 postmortem in 3 hours. create follow-up ticket 9001 and add owners. keep caps enabled until fix merges and gets canary validation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity SEV-2, follow-up ticket 9001 created.

sarah: thanks everyone. postmortem owners miguel+ben+sarah. bringing product & security into follow-up loop. :thumbsup:
